answer: Deal every identity one narrow live window per epoch on a public timetable — a pulse the whole network can hear. The operator must be present and answering inside that window, and windows are dealt so one operator's identities land on overlapping slots. An inlet admits only identities whose window was actually staffed. A farm of a hundred heads needs a hundred simultaneous operators, and timber — the slow, serial cost of real attention — is the one resource a script cannot clone. Miss your window twice and the identity goes dark for an epoch.
